News Items 
 
Lexington Twinning Group Visit 
The twinning between Kildare and Lexington Kentucky, was instigated in 1984 by 
then County Manager, Gerald Ward and has grown and been sustained through the 
Twinning Committee and Kildare County Council (see pages 11-13). 
 
NOAC Local Authority Performance Indicator Report 
In 2024, NOAC assessed 46 indicators spanning eleven key areas of local 
authorities’ diverse functions, with the aim of providing objective, data-driven insights 
into performance (see page 14). 
 
Mobile Library  
On 24 October 2025, Kildare Library Service signed a contract with Cahill Truck 
Bodies, Graignamanagh to build a new Mobile Library vehicle. 
This new mobile library will be custom-made with wheelchair access and is to be 
built with Climate Action and sustainability in mind (see page 15). 
 
Housing Delivery 
The tender process will be advertised in mid-November inviting proposals for the 
construction of new housing units on undeveloped sites and the completion of 
partially built housing schemes (see page 25). 
 
Staff Energy Awareness   
A Staff Energy Awareness Day took place on 29 October during Climate Action 
Week with experts attending from across the industry focusing on improving Home 
Energy (see page 62).

Tidy Towns 
Kildare’s Tidy Towns Groups performed extremely well in this years national Tidy 
Towns Competition with eleven towns winning a gold medal and Broadford winning a 
silver medal.  Naas was once again the county winner (see page 67). 
 
Maynooth Eastern Ring Road 
The letter of acceptance has issued for the Maynooth Eastern Ring Road to the 
successful contractor, John Cradock Limited. A prestart meeting has taken place 
with the contractor and a further update on the construction programme will be 
provided in due course (see page 70). 
 
Opening of Inclusive Playground at Station Road, Leixlip 
Kildare County Council announced the opening of a newly developed, fully inclusive 
playground at Station Road, Leixlip.  Designed to welcome children of all ages and 
abilities (see page 75). 
 
County Development Plan Actions 
A range of projects are being progressed, including Active Recreational 
Infrastructure Strategy, Strategic Employment Locations Study; Liffey Valley Park 
(Phase One) Feasibility Study; Corbally Canal Feasibility Study; and Landscape 
Character Assessment (see page 76). 
 
Into Kildare 
The highlight of October was the official opening of the Shackleton Experience in 
Athy. The museum provides an immersive experience that showcases original 
artefacts, personal letters and interactive exhibits, all of which bring Shackleton’s 
polar adventures to life (see pages 83-84). 
 
€1,000 Winter Retail Window Merchandising Grant  
The Winter Retail Window Merchandising Grant has opened for local businesses to 
apply for 50% grant aid (up to €1,000) to enhance their window displays for 
Christmas (see page 89).

Affordable Purchase - Barracksfield West, Naas 
The statutory notice issued for Barracksfield West, Naas on 04 November.  
The portal will open from 26 November until 17 December to accept applications 
(see page 26). 
 
The Community Integration Forum 
The Bi-monthly meeting of the Community Integration Forum (CIF) was held on 
Tuesday, 04 November. A further CIF meeting is scheduled for 09 December (see 
page 51). 
 
Brigid, Spirit of Kildare Programme 
The Brigid, Spirit of Kildare Festival 2026 was launched on the 23 October 
announcing headline act ‘Picture This’. The band will return to their home county of 
Kildare for an unmissable performance in the Dreamland Ballroom, Athy, on Friday, 
30 January 2026 (see page 52). 
 
Spirit of Kildare Awards 2026 
A new initiative, the Spirit of Kildare Awards 2026, was launched on 05 November 
2026.  The awards will shine a spotlight on people and organisations in Kildare 
whose actions, creativity, and commitment have made a meaningful difference to 
others. Nominations can be submitted online. The deadline for nominations is 
5.00pm, Thursday, 04 December 2025 (see page 53). 
 
Student Exchange Programme   
The 2026 Kildare-Lexington Student Exchange Programme is now open for 
applications.  The deadline for submission of applications is Friday, 05 December 
2025 (see page 54).

Council Ecocomic Development and National Paint Reuse Network to be a official

Executive Suite: 
Report on Visit to Lexington by 
group from Kildare from 20 to 25 
October 2025 for the 250th 
Celebrations 
 
Background: The twinning between 
Kildare and Lexington (Kentucky), was 
instigated in 1984 by then County 
Manager, Gerald Ward and has grown 
and been sustained through the 
Twinning Committee and Kildare 
County Council. The concept of 
twinning is about development and 
sustaining friendships between 
different parts the world and in this 
case is reflected in the work of the 
Kildare Twinning Committee chaired 
currently by Councillor Fintan Brett. 
The committee includes 
representatives of the local authority

_________________________________________________________________________________ 
 
Chief Executive Monthly Management Report – November 2025                       Page 13 of 93 
 
 
 
as well as members with long 
relationships with their counterparts in 
Lexington Sister Cities Committee. In 
addition to Kildare, Lexington is a 
Sister City with Shinhidaka in Japan, 
with Deauville in France and with 
Newmarket in the UK. In each case, 
the initial basis for the relationship was 
the strong equine tradition and 
industry. Originally based around the 
equine industry, our relationship has 
grown to include culture, industry and 
shared experiences. An example of 
this was how a visit to Lexington 
informed the approach to the 
Kerdiffstown regenerative parks 
project which recently saw Kildare 
County Council win “The Local 
Authority of the Year 2025” in the 
Green Transformation Awards.  
 
In September 2024, the Mayor of 
Lexington, Linda Gorton, extended a 
kind invitation to the Cathaoirleach and 
a delegation from Kildare County 
Council to join in the celebrations of 
Lexington’s two hundred and fiftieth 
Anniversary. Founded in 1775, just 
one year before the signing of the 
Declaration of Independence and the 
beginning of the American Revolution, 
Lexington has a long history and holds 
a unique place in the history of the 
United States. The programme for this 
visit in October 2025 was agreed 
through engagement between the 
offices of the Chief Executive of 
Kildare County Council and Ms. Kay 
Sargent, Executive Director of Sister 
Cities in Kentucky. The composition of 
the group was agreed by the Chief 
Executive and those who participated 
in the official visit were Carmel Kelly, 
Cathaoirleach, Sonya Kavanagh, Chief 
Executive, Alan Dunney, Director of 
Services. Councillors Veralouise 
Behan, Fintan Brett, Brian O’Loughlin, 
Angela Feeney, and Rupert Heather,  
 
Programme  
The programme of events included 
visits to Ashford Stud Farm: Ashford 
Stud, in the heart of Kentucky’s 
famous Bluegrass, is home to 
Coolmore America. There are many 
graduates of the Irish National Stud 
six-month residential course working in 
stud farms throughout Lexington and 
Kentucky. Alltech Biotechnology 
Company: Alltech was founded by 
biochemist Pearse Lyons in 1980 in 
Lexington, Kentucky. Pearse Lyons 
was born in Dundalk, Ireland and was 
educated in UCD. Dublin. In 1980, he

founded Alltech and the company 
began to supply biotechnology-derived 
ingredients to the livestock and poultry 
feed industry. The company opened its

Lexington Brewing Company. Makers 
Mark Distillery and RD1 Distillery: 
Bourbon Whiskey Distillers in

Attended a council meeting and the

Comments and Observations.  
It is clear that the twinning 
arrangement is hugely valued by the 
Sister Cities group in Lexington and 
that it should continue, to ensure the 
relationship is meaningful and 
valuable.  
The student exchange throughout the 
years has forged many friendships and 
connections between Kildare and 
Lexington that have continued into 
adulthood.  
In addition to the twinning committee in 
Lexington, there is a large and very 
active group of Friendship Volunteers 
who financially support and work with 
Kay to maintain strong bonds. They 
were available as volunteer drivers 
throughout the visit and involved in all 
aspects.  
It was wonderful to meet proud Irish 
people who are involved in various

Kildare Readers Festival 2025 
The Kildare Readers’ Festival 2025 
took place from 04 to 14 October. A 
celebration of books, ideas, and 
conversation – bringing readers and 
writers together in a warm and 
welcoming space. We hosted a total of 
sixteen events with a combined 
attendance of 795. 
With a programme that spanned 
fiction, poetry, politics, memoir, and 
more, this year’s festival offered 
something for every reader. 
From debut voices to literary icons via 
workshops to lively panels, we 
explored the stories that shape, 
challenge, and connect us!

“Dads Fest” Newbridge and Clane 
Kildare Library Service was delighted 
to be involved with Dads Fest again 
this year. Dads Fest is an interagency 
initiative of the Kildare and West 
Wicklow Forum. It seeks to engage 
dads more with our services, providing 
support and a social outlet for Dads to 
come together with their children. Two 
great days were held in Clane GAA 
and Newbridge Family Resource 
Centre on 05 and 19 October with 
activities such as drumming, baby 
beats, crafts, slime workshops, 
facepainting and sensory play. 155 
Dads attended with their children over 
the course of the two days and great 
feedback was received. 
 
Mobile Library  
 
On 24 October 2025, Kildare Library 
Service signed a contract with Cahill 
Truck Bodies, Graignamanagh, County 
Kilkenny to build a new Mobile Library 
vehicle. 
 
This new mobile library will be custom-
made with wheelchair access and is to 
be built with Climate Action and 
sustainability in mind including 
features such as energy-efficient LED 
lighting, PV solar panels on the roof 
and will operate on hydrotreated 
vegetable oil (HVO) to lower the 
vehicle’s carbon emissions.

Computer Beginner Classes 
Celbridge and Leixlip libraries recently 
completed a five-week beginner-level 
computer course for adults, facilitated 
by Searsol. These classes were made 
possible through funding from Kildare 
County Council, following a motion 
raised at a Celbridge-Leixlip Municipal 
District meeting. The sessions were 
well attended and covered a range of 
practical digital skills, including Safe 
online shopping, paying tolls 
electronically, Managing taxes online 
and much more. 
The initiative aimed to empower adults 
with essential IT skills for everyday 
tasks, promoting digital inclusion and 
confidence in using technology. 
 
Adult Literacy for Life  
HSE/ EVE Larine Maynooth partnered 
with Kildare Libraries Service to offer a 
ten-week course on Health Literacy 
and Digital Literacy.  
The course was funded under Adult 
Literacy for Life (ALL) funding.  
During the course, participants 
covered a diverse range of topics 
including: making health decisions; 
evaluating health websites; reading 
labels and instructions; accessing 
medication and doctors online. A 
personal health passport booklet was 
also produced as part of the course. A 
mental health nurse also came in as 
part of the course to answer questions. 
 
Climate Action

collaborated with the Climate Action 
Office of Kildare County Council to 
host an information session in the 
library on Community Climate Action 
Programme Grants, a scheme under

have a direct climate action impact. 
Maynooth Community Library also 
launched a new climate themed book 
club, which was launched by Sadhbh 
O' Neill, environmental and climate 
activist, researcher, lecturer and 
contributor to the Irish Times opinion 
and environment pages.

Local Authority Integration Team 
(LAIT) 
The LAIT is part of a national 
government policy - White Paper to 
end direct provision (February 2021) - 
and a new international protection 
service model grounded on supporting 
the principles of ‘integration from day 
one’. To this end, a permanent 
network of Local Authority Integration 
Teams was established across Ireland 
in all local authorities (31 LAIT in total) 
to support persons seeking 
international protection in Ireland; 
persons with status; temporary 
protection; or participating in the Irish 
Refugee Protection Programme. The 
LAIT act as mentors and connectors 
with local services including:  
 
· Being a direct contact for new 
arrivals, offering information, 
advice, and guidance through often 
complex public services, facilitating 
access to services appropriate to 
needs, and helping to resolve 
barriers when dealing with public 
services.  
 
· Connecting new arrivals with local 
services that improve their ability to 
build independent lives in a new 
country, like job training, English 
classes, education, and 
apprenticeships. 
 
· Offering guidance through the 
process of applying for healthcare, 
financial budgeting and support, 
and other services they might 
need. 
 
· Identifying gaps in supports and 
services, working collaboratively to 
create efficient and well-
coordinated integration systems, 
including efficient needs 
assessment, or strong inter-agency 
collaboration.  
 
· Supporting people if they face 
racism or unfair treatment. 
 
The Local Authority Integration Teams 
are a strong example of how 
integration policy can be turned into 
practical, people-centred action that 
supports newcomers from the moment 
they arrive navigating new civic 
systems. Structured support through 
the LAIT model strengthens 
newcomers’ sense of belonging and 
fosters social cohesion, while 
demonstrating how national funding
